headline: What Does
the FOMC
Actually Do?
In 3 Steps
slides.subtitle:
The committee behind
the Fed's rate decisions.

slides.title: In One Sentence
slides.big: The FOMC is the Fed committee that votes on interest rate policy.
slides.body: It has 12 voting members and meets about eight times a year.

slides.title: How It Works
items: Members review data on jobs and prices.
They vote on a target range for the rate.
The Fed publishes a statement after the vote.
slides.disclaimer: For informational purposes only. Not investment advice.

slides.title: Why It Matters to You
slides.body: FOMC decisions can shape borrowing costs, from mortgages and car loans to credit cards, and the interest you earn on savings.

slides.title: Remember This
items: The FOMC sets the Fed's rate target.
It votes about eight times a year.
